quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs and other road rules are rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When traveling in a group, riders should:

options.text: Spread out to make the group easier to see.
Stay close together to make the group easier to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay close together to make the group easier to see.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, stay close together but leave enough space around each rider. This makes the group easier to see and keeps riders from getting separated. Riding in pairs does not give riders enough room to move safely.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a good safety tip?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before turning.
When turning, lean in the direction you wish to go.
Avoid dragging your feet on the roadway.

questions.explanation: Slow down before turning and lean in the direction you are turning. Do not drag your feet on the road, as they could catch on something and cause you to lose control. Always watch for other traffic.

questions.question: The effects of marijuana consumption can last for:
questions.explanation: When smoked, marijuana can affect you within minutes and effects last two to four hours. When eaten, it may take over an hour to start working, but effects can last more than six hours.

questions.question: How does the stopping distance for motorcycles compare to the stopping distance for cars?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need a little longer to stop.
Both motorcycles and cars take about the same amount of time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both motorcycles and cars take about the same amount of time to stop.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, motorcycles and cars stop in about the same distance. However, wet or slippery roads make it much harder for motorcycles to stop quickly.

questions.question: When riding under normal conditions, maintain a minimum following distance of:
questions.explanation: Keep at least four seconds of distance behind the vehicle in front of you during normal conditions. Increase this distance if conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: Which of the following is a poor reason to sound your horn?

options.text: A driver in the lane next to you is too close to the vehicle ahead of them.
A parked car has a person in the driver's seat.
You want people to look at your motorcycle.
You are passing someone who is in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to look at your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sound your horn to alert vehicles or pedestrians before you pass them. If you see a driver in the next lane riding too close to the car ahead, they may try to move into your lane. Alert pedestrians or bicyclists in the street as you pass. Do not use your horn just to get attention.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Prevent access to an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent access to an escape route.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It keeps you away from other drivers' blind spots and surface hazards. Your position should give you an escape route if a danger appears. It should not block your escape route.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn both your head and your shoulders to get a better look.
Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Only move your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn your head but not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level.

questions.question: A front tire blowout is especially dangerous because:

options.text: The front part of the motorcycle will be lower than usual.
The rear brake cannot be used.
The front brake cannot be used.

questions.explanation: A front tire blowout is dangerous because it makes steering difficult. You will know your front tire has failed if the steering suddenly feels heavy.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the brake until the tire grips again, then brake again.
Release the brake and use only the front brake.
Keep the brake locked until the motorcycle stops.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the brake locked until the motorcycle stops.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while braking, do not release the brake. Keep it locked until the motorcycle comes to a complete stop.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should you do?

options.text: Put inexperienced riders at the back of the group.
Do not ride too close to other riders in the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not ride too close to other riders in the group.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, use a staggered formation and check your mirrors often. The lead and sweep riders should be experienced. Keep enough space between yourself and other riders.

questions.question: Of crashes between a motorcycle and a car, how many are caused by the car driver failing to yield the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle-car crashes happen because the car driver fails to yield the right-of-way to the rider.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, what should you do?

options.text: Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
Press the handle grip in the opposite direction of where you want to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve, apply light pressure to the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then press the right to straighten. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: Which vest or jacket color helps you be seen the most?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors while riding to be more visible. Bright red, orange, yellow, or green are best. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what does the lead rider mean by raising their left arm and extending their index finger?

options.text: The group will exit at the next exit.

questions.explanation: Hand signals are used to communicate in group riding. When the lead rider raises their left arm and extends their index finger, the group should move into a single-file formation.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you will slow down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down suddenly. This warns a tailgater who may not see hazards ahead that you are slowing down.

questions.question: To carry a passenger safely, you may need to adjust:
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight. You may need to adjust the shocks to handle this weight. Also adjust the headlight and mirrors because the motorcycle will sit at a different angle.

questions.question: When packing items on a motorcycle, where should heavier items go?

options.text: In front of you with lighter items behind.

questions.explanation: Pack heavier items toward the front of your load. Place the load over or in front of the rear axle. Lighter items should be packed behind you.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What is true about motorcycle windshields?

options.text: They work as well as a face shield.
They work as well as goggles.
They do not protect your eyes from wind.
They protect against objects thrown from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They do not protect your eyes from wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield is not a good replacement for a face shield or goggles. Most windshields cannot protect your eyes from wind.

questions.question: When carrying a heavy load on your motorcycle, you should adjust the:
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to match the recommended settings for that weight.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.
questions.explanation: At any speed, riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets.

questions.question: The center of a lane usually has an oily strip. This area is:

options.text: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny.
Always safe, no matter the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip in the center of lanes. When the road is dry, this area has enough traction for safe motorcycle riding. The strip is usually only two feet wide, so you can ride to one side of it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: When riding through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.
